grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Genesis 1:24-27 creates the animals first, and finally man: male and female he creates them. Genesis 2:7 and 2:18-22 tell of another command: God forms man from dust, then forms the animals and brings them to the man, and only then takes the woman from the rib. Apologists' answer: Chapter 2 is not a second chronology, but a close on the human being within the sixth day.
aprofundar: What the research says: Most scholars see here two texts of different origins stitched side by side. The first, called priestly, speaks of Elohim, God, solemnly and organized in days. The second, called the Javits, speaks of the Lord God, Yahweh, intimately and artistically. Whoever edited Genesis didn't hide the differences; he kept the two voices. Inner reading: Perhaps the Bible itself teaches that no single narrative exhausts the mystery.
camada3: To reflect: If ancient publishers accepted two versions side by side, why is a single literal reading required today?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Matthew 27:5 says that Judas threw the coins into the sanctuary and went to hang himself, and Matthew 27:7 says that the priests used them to buy the potter's field. Acts 1:18 says that he himself acquired a field and, rushing in, fell on his face and burst open in the middle. Answer of the apologists: he hanged himself, the rope or twig yielded and the body fell, and the field bought by the priests with his money was attributed to him.
aprofundar: What the research says: Many scholars see two independent traditions about the end of the traitor, both linked to a real place in Jerusalem, the Field of Blood, each with a different tone. Matthew reads the scene in the light of the prophets; Luke, the author of Acts, in the light of the punishment of betrayers. Internal reading: The early Christians were not concerned with standardizing accounts; they were concerned with wanting a Bible without history.
camada3: To ponder: Do two different memories of the same event make the event less real, or just more human?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Matthew 1:16 says: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary. Luke 3:23 says that Jesus was, as it were, the son of Joseph, the son of Heli. The two Gospels give different ancestries for Jesus, and the lists follow differently to David. Apologists' answer: Luke would bring the lineage of Mary, or a law of levirate marriage would make Joseph have a biological father and a legal one, an explanation given by Julius Africanus in the third century.
aprofundar: What the research says: Ancient genealogies were more theological than papyrus. Matthew organizes the list into three blocks of fourteen generations, linking Jesus to Abraham and David; Luke goes up to Adam, linking Jesus to all mankind. The expression how he was cared for in Luke already shows that the writer knew that Joseph was not the biological father in his belief. Inner reading: Each gospel tells who Jesus is to his community.
camada3: To ponder: Is your identity in the names of your ancestors or in what you do with what you have received?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Who instigated David - God or Satan?
palavras: who instigated david - god or satan
resposta: 2 Samuel 24:1 says that the anger of the Lord was kindled and the Lord moved David to number Israel. 1 Chronicles 21:1, recounting the same event, says: Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to number Israel. Apologists' Answer: God allowed Satan to act, so each scripture highlights one side of the same action.
aprofundar: What research says: Chronicles was written centuries after Samuel, after the Babylonian exile, when the figure of an adversary, Satan, was gaining strength in Jewish thought. The chronicler seems to have avoided attributing to God an act that led to a plague. It's a rare example of seeing theology change within the Bible itself. Inner reading: Our idea of God grows over time, and the Bible records that growth.
camada3: To think about it: When something bad happens, do you blame God, the devil, or human choices? And who taught you to pick?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: 1 Samuel 17:50 says that David defeated the Philistine with a sling and a stone. 2 Samuel 21:19 says: "El-hanan the son of Jaare-orim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite. And 1 Chronicles 20:5 says that El-hanan killed Lamech, the brother of Goliath. Apologists' answer: There was a copying error in 2 Samuel, and Chronicles preserves the correct reading; so some translations add Goliath's brother in 2 Samuel.
aprofundar: What the research says: Many scholars think otherwise, that the earliest tradition attributed the victory to El-hanan, a warrior of David, and that fame later passed to the king, as with national heroes. Chronicles, later, would have harmonized. Note that in the Almeida quoted here, 2 Samuel 21:19 does not use the word brother. Inner reading: hero stories grow; this applies to all peoples.
camada3: To contemplate: Which giants in your life have you toppled, and who took the credit?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
palavras: how many angels in the tomb
resposta: Matthew 28:1-2: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary; an angel descends and sits on the stone. Mark 16:1-5: three women; the stone has already been rolled away and a young man is sitting inside. Luke 24:1-4 and 24:10: several women and two men. John 20:1 and 20:11-12: Mary Magdalene alone in the dark, followed by two angels. The apologists' answer: the accounts complete each other, each mentions part of the people, and the differences show independent testimonies, not a composite story.
aprofundar: What the survey says: The four agree on the center: the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene, and the empty tomb. The details vary as in oral traditions that circulated for decades before they were written down. Historians like Bart Ehrman and apologists like Michael Licona discuss these same differences with conflicting conclusions about what they mean. Inner reading: What faith affirms, the resurrection, is an affirmation of faith; what history shows is that the first followers believed it deeply.
camada3: To ponder, why are the first witnesses in the four accounts women, at a time when their testimony was of little value?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Mark 14:12 places the Last Supper on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover was slaughtered; that is, Jesus eats the Passover meal and dies the next day. John 18:28 says that on the morning of the trial the accusers had not yet eaten the passover, and John 19:14 says: it was the preparation of the passover. In John, Jesus dies before the Passover meal. Apologists' Answer: Jewish groups used different calendars, or the word passover in John refers to the entire week of the feast.
aprofundar: What the research says: Many scholars see here a theological choice by John: Jesus dies at the time the Passover lambs were sacrificed in the temple, and is called, at John 1:29, the Lamb of God. Mark and the others turn the Passover meal into the first Christian supper. They both wanted to say something real to them, and the calendar served that purpose. Inner reading: the gospels are testimonies of faith, not police ties.
camada3: To contemplate: What weighs more heavily on you, the exact date of an event or the meaning it took in the life of the one who lived it?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
palavras: what jesus said on the cross
oh, my god, why did you abandon me
o que jesus disse na cruz
deus meu por que me desamparaste
resposta: Mark 15:34: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Luke 23:46: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit". John 19:30: It is finished. Each gospel records a different last sentence. Apologists' answer: Jesus said several phrases on the cross, and each author recorded one; tradition brings together the seven words of the cross.
aprofundar: What the research says: there is no necessary logical contradiction here, but there are three portraits: in Mark, the anguish of abandonment, quoting Psalm 22; in Luke, the serene trust; in John, the mission accomplished. Inside reading: the three attitudes fit into a human life, and maybe that's why all three were saved. Honesty: not every difference is a contradiction, and the Portal doesn't inflate differences.
camada3: To contemplate: in the face of your greatest pains, which of these three phrases is closest to your heart today?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Genesis 6:6 says: "Jehovah felt regret that he had made the man". In 1 Samuel 15:11, God says, "I regret that I made Saul king". But Numbers 23:19 says that God is not a man to repent, and the same chapter at 1 Samuel 15:29 repeats: He does not lie or repent. Apologists' Answer: Repentance is a human language to describe God's reaction to human choices, not a change in his being.
aprofundar: What the research says: The Hebrew Bible paints two images of God side by side: a very close God who feels, grieves, and changes his plans, and an unchanging God who is above emotions. Later theology, influenced by Greek philosophy, favored the latter. Inside reading: Both images speak of real experiences of faith: that of a caring God and that of a God who does not fail.
camada3: To ponder: Would you prefer a God who feels for you or a God who never changes? Why not both?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: James 1:13 says: "When under trial, let no one say: 'I am being tried by God.' Genesis 22:1 says that God tested Abraham by asking him to sacrifice Isaac; the Hebrew word, nissah, can mean to test or tempt, and several ancient translations use tempted. Apologists' answer: Proving to strengthen is not the same as trying to lead to evil, and James speaks of the latter.
aprofundar: What the research says: here the contradiction depends on the translation. The Almeida quoted uses proved, which already resolves some of the tension. The case teaches something important: Many famous contradictions arise or add up in translation, and checking the original is a student's duty. Inner reading: Being tested is a universal human experience; the question is what do we do with it?
camada3: To think about it, did a trial you experienced strengthen you or hurt you? And who decided its direction?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: 2 Kings 8:26 says that Ahaziah was 22 years old when he began to reign. 2 Chronicles 22:2 in the Almeida says: he was forty-two years old. As his father Jehoram began to reign at thirty-two and reigned eight years, according to 2 Kings 8:17, he died at forty; a son of forty-two would be impossible. Apologists' Answer: It is a copying error in Chronicles; the Bible is inspired by the original, and copies may have errors.
aprofundar: What the research says: The ancient Greek translation, the Septuagint, and the Syriac have twenty-two in Chronicles, and so several modern Bibles already correct the number. It's a clear example of a transmission error, recognized even by conservative scholars. Inner reading: The Bible we have has passed through thousands of hands; knowing this does not destroy faith, it destroys the idea that anyone has the right to use it as if it had fallen ready from heaven.
camada3: To reflect: If the church itself admits copying errors, why do so many leaders speak as if every comma were dictated by God?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Do children pay for their parents?
palavras: do children pay for their parents
resposta: Exodus 20:5 says: I visit the iniquity of the fathers upon the sons to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me. Deuteronomy 24:16 says: "Children should not be put to death for their fathers; each one should die for his own sin". And Ezekiel 18:20: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. Apologists' answer: Exodus speaks of the consequences that pass through generations who persist in the same error, and Deuteronomy speaks of human courts.
aprofundar: What the research says: Ezekiel writes in exile, when the people repeated the proverb quoted at 18:2, the parents ate green grapes, and the children's teeth became dull, and the prophet rejects him head-on. It's a moral correction within the Bible itself. Inside reading: Ezekiel 18 is one of the best remedies against the hereditary curse preaching, which uses Exodus 20 to generate fear and sell curse breaking.
camada3: To reflect: What family guilt do you bear without having committed it? Ezekiel would say she's not yours.

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, it is God who acts. Genesis 6:7: I will wipe out man whom I have created from the surface of the ground, both man and beast. Genesis 7:23 And all flesh was destroyed from off the earth; and only Noah remained, and those that were with him in the ark. Apologists' answer: It was a righteous judgment, because the earth was corrupt and filled with violence, as Genesis 6:11 says, and God saved those who would listen.
aprofundar: What the research says: stories of a flood sent by the gods exist before the Bible in Mesopotamia, as in the Epic of Gilgamesh and the myth of Atrahasis, with the ark, animals and even the bird loose to find land. Geology finds no sign of a recent global flood. Many theologians read the account as a theological narrative about evil and a new beginning. Inner reading: The moral question remains: What does it mean to worship a God thus described? The Bible does not hide the question.
camada3: To contemplate: How many children were outside the ark? The Bible does not say, but the question is yours, and it is legitimate.
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, it is God who acts. Genesis 19:24-25: Jehovah rained sulphur and fire from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah, and overturned those cities and all their inhabitants. Apologists' answer: Rather, at Genesis 18:32, God agrees to spare the city if there are ten righteous ones, showing that the punishment was not arbitrary.
aprofundar: What the research says: The Bible text itself, at Ezekiel 16, at 16:49, points to Sodom's wickedness: pride, plenty of bread, and never strengthening the hand of the poor and needy. Archaeologists debate whether the story holds the memory of an actual destruction near the Dead Sea; there is no consensus. Inside reading: Abraham's negotiation with God is one of the boldest scenes in the Bible: a man questioning divine justice, and being heard.
camada3: For contemplation: Abraham had the courage to ask God if he was righteous. Who taught you that asking is a sin?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
palavras: the death of egypt s firstborn
deus endureceu o coracao de farao
resposta: In the text, it is God who acts. Exodus 12:29: At midnight Jehovah struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn to the firstborn of the bondman in the dungeon. And Exodus 9:12 says that the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart. Apologists' answer: Pharaoh first hardened his own heart, as Exodus 8:15 says, and before that he had ordered the Hebrew boys to be thrown into the river, at Exodus 1:22; the plague was judgment on an oppressive empire.
aprofundar: What the research says: There is no Egyptian record of the plagues or of a mass exodus, and many archaeologists feel that the story preserves, in epic form, the memory of smaller groups leaving Egypt. The moral tension is in the text itself: the prisoner's son, who decided nothing, also dies. Jewish tradition, at Passover, spills drops of wine for each plague, a reminder of the suffering of the Egyptians. Inside reading: even the feast of liberation keeps a gesture of compassion for the enemy.
camada3: To ponder: Has your release ever cost anyone pain? Can you remember that without losing your joy?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, it is a command attributed to God. Deuteronomy 20:16-17: Of the cities of these nations thou shalt let nothing that breatheth live; thou shalt utterly destroy them, as Jehovah thy God hath commanded thee. Joshua 6:21, in Jericho: they destroyed with the edge of the sword man and woman, young and old. The apologists' answer: it was exaggerated war language, common in the ancient East, and a judgment on specific peoples, not a model for today, as Paul Copan argues.
aprofundar: What the research says: Archaeology does not confirm a quick and total conquest. Jericho was virtually uninhabited at the probable time, and many scholars see Israel emerging gradually from within the Canaanite population itself. I mean, the massacre may never have happened like this, but the text that celebrates it exists, and it's been used throughout history to justify conquests, including against indigenous peoples in the Americas. Inner reading: The danger is not just in the past of the text; it is in whoever uses it today to say that God is on the side of their war.
camada3: To reflect: If someone today told you that God ordered the extermination of a people, would you believe him? Why would the ancient text be any different?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, it is a command attributed to God through the prophet Samuel. 1 Samuel 15:3: strike Amalek and destroy it completely; you shall kill men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep. The reason given at 15:2 is what Amalek did to Israel centuries earlier at the exodus from Egypt. Saul loses his kingdom for not keeping his promises. Apologists' answer: Amalek was a recidivist aggressor people, and the total language is war hyperbole.
aprofundar: What the research says: this is one of the most difficult texts for Christian and Jewish theology itself. Rabbis over the centuries have restricted it to the point of making it inapplicable, and many theologians frankly say that it reflects the war mentality of the day, not the will of God as revealed in Jesus. Inner reading: the text punishes Saul for having spared; human conscience today punishes the opposite. That tension is the question the portal will answer.
camada3: To contemplate: Can a child bear the guilt of what his people did four hundred years ago?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Here the text mixes two voices, and you have to separate them. Numbers 31:1-2: God tells Moses to avenge the sons of Israel of the Midianites. The harshest command comes from Moses, a human, in 31:15-18: kill all the boys and all the women who have known a man; but the virgin girls, let them live for yourselves. Apologists' answer: It was judgment by the seduction of Peor, and captives were taken as wives under laws that prohibited selling them, such as Deuteronomy 21:10-14.
aprofundar: What the research says: The text does not say that God commanded the killing of the boys; it is Moses who is indignant and gives the order, and the chapter goes on without reproach, counting at 31:35 thirty-two thousand virgin girls among the spoils. Many scholars read the chapter as a late, priestly composition with no historical confirmation. Even the law of Deuteronomy 21, which forbids the sale of the captive, presupposes a woman taken by force after the death of her family. Inner reading: Honesty is not softening the text nor attributing to God what the text attributes to Moses.
camada3: To contemplate: what happened to those girls? The Bible doesn't say. Silence is also a text.
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: The bears and the forty-two boys
palavras: the bears and the forty-two boys
resposta: 2 Kings 2:23-24: Some boys mocked Elisha, saying, "Go up, bald man!" And he cursed them in the name of Jehovah; and two bears came out of the woods, and tore forty-two of them to pieces. The text does not say that God sent the bears; it links the curse made in the name of the Lord to the attack. Apologists' answer: The Hebrew word translated boys, naar, can mean boys or young men, and mockery would be a threatening rejection of God's prophet.
aprofundar: What the research says: Elisha's stories form a cycle of prophetic legends that show the power of the man of God, and this serves as a warning: Don't mock the prophet. It is the exact same do not touch anointed one mechanism used today. Inside Reading: Jesus, when his disciples wanted to send fire from heaven upon a town that rejected him, rebuked them, as recorded at Luke 9:54-55. Within the Bible itself, one story corrects another.
camada3: To reflect: What fear is planted in a child when he hears that mocking a preacher brings divine punishment?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, it is God who acts. 2 Samuel 6:6-7: the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah stretched out his hand and took hold of the ark; and the anger of Jehovah was kindled, and God smote him there; and Uzzah died there by the ark. Apologists' answer: The law commanded that no one touch sacred things, lest he die, as at Numbers 4:15, and the ark was not even to be in an ox cart.
aprofundar: What the research says: The text itself records the human reaction, at 6:8-11: David was saddened, feared the Lord and left the ark in the house of Obed-Edom for three months. Many readers here see the ancient idea of the sacred as a dangerous, almost electric force that admits no contact. Inside reading: Uzzah wanted to protect the sacred and died; how many people today live in fear that a wrong gesture will condemn them?
camada3: To ponder: Does your God punish a good intention for a rule error? If so, who designed that God for you?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Death by Stoning in the Law
palavras: death by stoning in the law
resposta: In the text, they are commands attributed to God. Numbers 15:32-36: A man who gathers wood on the sabbath, of whom Jehovah had said to Moses, shall surely be put to death; and all the congregation shall stone him. Deuteronomy 21:18-21: the stubborn and rebellious son, a glutton and a drunkard, brought by his parents to the elders, would be stoned to death. Apologists' Answer: They were civil laws of ancient Israel, which Jesus fulfilled and surpassed, and do not apply to Christians.
aprofundar: What the research says: The rabbis of the Talmud themselves, in their treatise Sanhedrin, surrounded the law of the prodigal son with so many conditions that they concluded: There has never been and never will be a prodigal son so condemned. Jewish tradition already read the Law with interpretation and mercy. Internal reading: a text is only dangerous when its context is ripped out and its interpretation removed. The death penalty for a disobedient son, uttered today from the pulpit as a threat, is manipulation.
camada3: To reflect: If rabbis already softened this law two thousand years ago, why would anyone today use their handwriting to scare a child?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: In the text, they are laws attributed to God. Leviticus 25:44-46: from the foreigners you shall buy male and female slaves; you shall leave them as an inheritance to your children, forever. Exodus 21:20-21: if a master strikes his servant with a rod and the servant survives a day or two, he shall not be punished, for the servant is his money. Apologists' Answer: Ancient slavery was different from modern slavery, the Law regulated it without approving it, and Exodus 21:16 punished by death anyone who kidnapped and sold a person.
aprofundar: What the research says: These verses were quoted by pastors and theologians in the United States and Brazil in defense of African slavery, and that is exactly why the Southern Baptist Convention was born in 1845. Christian abolitionists responded in the spirit of the Gospel, such as Galatians 3:28. Both sides quoted the Bible; what changed was the conscience. Internal reading: a text does not defend itself; one must ask who the reading serves.
camada3: To reflect: If the Bible was used to enslave and to set free, what determines the use - the text or the heart of the reader?
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Job and the Gamble with Satan
palavras: job and the gamble with satan
o senhor deu e o senhor tirou
resposta: In the text, the one who acts is Satan, but with God's permission. Job 1:12: the Lord said to Satan, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on him. At 1:18-19, a strong wind collapses the house and kills Job's sons and daughters. And Job answers, in 1:21: The Lord hath given, and the Lord hath taken away. The apologists' answer: the book does not explain suffering, it shows that faith can cross it, and in the end God answers Job from the whirlwind.
aprofundar: What the research says: Job is a work of wisdom, probably a poetic parable, not a chronicle. Its center is a protest: Job questions God for dozens of chapters, and at the end, in Job 42:7, God says to his accusing friends: You have not spoken about me what is upright, as my servant Job has. Inside reading: The oldest book on suffering defends the right to complain to God, and condemns religious who blame the victim.
camada3: To contemplate: Job's ten children died in a bet. Do you accept this story as it is, as a parable, or as fact? Every reading changes your God.
parte: Atrocidades: ordenadas ou feitas por Deus no texto

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Here there is no command of God: the vow is of a man. Judges 11:30-31: Jephthah promises that the first one who comes out of his house to meet him will be a burnt offering. His only daughter comes out. At 11:39 he fulfilled in her the vow that he had made; and she had not known a man. Apologists' answer: Many, from medieval rabbis like David Kimchi, argue that she was consecrated to celibacy and not killed, and God never asked for this vow.
aprofundar: What the research says: Most scholars read the text as a real human sacrifice, narrated as the tragedy of a hasty vow. The text neither approves nor condemns him, and the Letter to the Hebrews, at 11:32, lists Jephthah among the heroes of faith. The daughter is unnamed; at 11:40 p.m., the daughters of Israel went yearly to mourn her for four days. Inside reading: How many religious promises, made in despair, have been paid for with the lives of those who promised nothing?
camada3: Consider: Jephthah's daughter is not named in the text. What name would you give her, and what would you say to her?
parte: Atrocidades: narradas como feitas por humanos

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Narrated as done by humans. Judges 19:25-29: To protect himself, the Levite hands over his concubine to the men of Gibeah, who molest her all night. In the morning she falls at the door with her hands on the threshold. He says, get up, let's go; she doesn't answer. At home, he cuts her into twelve pieces and sends them throughout Israel. Apologists' response: Judges describes, not approves; the book shows the moral collapse of a people without a king, as it repeats its end.
aprofundar: What the research says: Theologian Phyllis Trible called this and other accounts horror texts, and she called for them to be read in memory of the victims. The book closes at Judges 21:25: In those days there was no king in Israel; each one did what was right in his own eyes. The narrator criticizes anarchy; but the silence about the woman's pain is total. Inner reading: reading these texts is an act of memory; hiding them from the pulpit is choosing which victims deserve to be remembered.
camada3: To reflect: The Bible does not give this woman a voice. Reading her story to the end is one way to give her that voice back.
parte: Atrocidades: narradas como feitas por humanos

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: The War Against Benjamin and the Kidnapping of the Girls of Shiloh
palavras: the war against benjamin and the kidnapping of the girls of shiloh
resposta: Narrated as done by humans. After the crime of Gibeah, the tribes attack Benjamin; in Judges 20:28, they consult the Lord, who answers, "Come up". But what follows is the decision of the assembly: at 20:46-48, they kill men and animals and burn the cities; at 21:10-12, they have all in Jabesh-gilead killed, sparing four hundred virgins; and at 21:20-23, they have the Benjamites ambush and take away the dancing girls of Shiloh. Apologists' response: The book ends by showing, on purpose, how far a people without law and without king can go.
aprofundar: What the research says: Scholars read the end of Judges as a propaganda for monarchy: Without a king, everything would be chaos. To repair one massacre, the people commit another, and to restore women, they authorize a kidnapping. Honesty: The first battle has divine approval in the text; the extermination of Jabesh and the abduction of Shiloh are human decisions, and the text does not say that God commanded them. Inner reading: one unresolved violence breeds another, when no one has the courage to stop.
camada3: To reflect: Have you ever seen a community, or a family, trying to right a wrong with another wrong?
parte: Atrocidades: narradas como feitas por humanos

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Narrated as done by a human, and condemned by God in the text. 2 Samuel 11:14-15: David writes to Joab, places Uriah at the front where the fighting is fierce, and withdraws from him, so that he may be wounded and die, and sends the letter by the hand of Uriah himself. At 12:9, the prophet Nathan accuses: Uriah the Hittite you have killed with the sword, and his wife you have taken. Apologists' answer: The Bible does not hide the sin of its heroes, and Psalm 51 shows David's repentance.
aprofundar: What the research says: Many scholars and theologians point out that Bath-sheba, summoned by the most powerful king in the land, could hardly have refused, and that the text blames David, not her. Nathan is a rare role model: a religious man who confronts power and says, that man is you, at 12:7. Inside reading: The anointed David also erred, and the prophet did not keep quiet. This text is the best antidote against not touching the anointed one.
camada3: To contemplate: Who is Nathan in your life, the person who has the courage to tell you the truth?

resposta: Narrated as done by a human. 2 Samuel 13:14: Amnon the son of David would not listen to the voice of Tamar his half sister, and being stronger than she, he violated her and lay with her. Then he drove her out. At 13:21, when David learned of it, his anger was greatly kindled, but the text records no punishment of his son. aprofundar: What the research says: Tamar is one of the few victims who speaks in the text: she argues, pleads, resists, and then tears her clothes and places ashes on her head in public. The father's silence, which does not punish, has been read by many theologians as the portrait of family cover-up. the evolution of the image of jehovah
resposta: Academic research shows that the image of God changes throughout the Bible. Deuteronomy 32:8-9 says in the Almeida: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel; for the portion of the Lord is his people. But one of the Dead Sea Scrolls and the ancient Greek translation bring forth children of God, not of Israel. Apologists' Answer: The sons of God would be angels guarding the nations, under the one true God.
aprofundar: What the research says: Scholars such as Mark Smith and Thomas Römer, author of The Invention of God, read in this verse the memory of a time when the Most High, El, divided the nations among lesser gods, and Yahweh received Israel. Javé would have been a warrior and storm god coming from the south, then merged with El. Eighth-century B.C.E. inscriptions found at Kuntillet Ajrud in Sinai bless in the name of Yahweh and his Asherah, a sign that many Israelites worshipped a goddess besides Yahweh. Strict monotheism, one God and no other, took hold around the time of the Babylonian exile in the sixth century before Christ. Seal: What the manuscripts bring is proven; the reconstruction of Yahweh's story is a strong scholarly hypothesis. Inner reading: Israel's faith matured, and the Bible preserves the layers of that path.
camada3: To reflect: If God's image evolved within the Bible itself, can it continue to evolve within you?

resposta: About the year 144, Marcion, a wealthy Christian in Rome, taught that the righteous, warrior God of the Old Testament was not the loving Father announced by Jesus. He compiled the first Christian list of sacred books, without the Old Testament, and wrote the Antitheses, contrasting, for example, an eye for an eye from Exodus with the offering the other side of Matthew 5:38-39. Church Response: Marcion was declared a heretic, and the church affirmed that there is one God in both testaments.
aprofundar: What Gnostic tradition says: Texts found at Nag Hammadi speak of a demiurge, a lesser, ignorant creator, sometimes called Yaldabaoth, who claims to be the only god. That is Gnostic tradition, attributed to her, not fact. What is a historical fact is that Marcion's question of how the God of Joshua could be the Father of Jesus never ceased to be asked, and the reaction to it helped the Church to define its canon. Inner reading: Whoever asks this today is not the first; they are in a conversation almost two thousand years old.
camada3: To think about it: Have you also felt that the God you have been taught does not match the Jesus you read about? What do you do with that?

resposta: 1 John 4:8 says: "God is love". And Jesus, at Matthew 5:43-44, says: "You heard that it was said, 'You must hate your enemy; but I say to you, Love your enemies.' How do you reconcile that with the war texts? Theology offers many answers, and the Portal presents them all without choosing for you.
aprofundar: Key answers attributed to their proponents: Origen, in the third century, read violent texts as an allegory of spiritual struggle. Progressive revelation says that God revealed himself gradually, adapted to the mindset of each age, right down to Jesus. Paul Copan argues that the language of war is exaggeration typical of the ancient East. Gregory Boyd, in The Crucifixion of the Warrior God, 2017, argues that the cross is the lens, and that where the text contradicts the love of Christ, it reflects the authors' limited vision. But verses 9 to 14 show who the psalm speaks of - Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who wandered from nation to nation, and God rebuked kings to protect them. The wearer's answer: The leader is anointed and can only be judged by God.
aprofundar: The context teaches the opposite of usage: the psalm protects frail people from powerful kings, not powerful ones from questions. In the Bible, the prophet Nathan confronts anointed King David, and Paul resists Peter in person at Galatians 2:11. Acts 17:11 commends those who examined the Scriptures to see if what Paul himself said was true. This use has a name: proof-texting, pulling a verse out of context to prove what you already wanted. How to protect yourself: Always read the entire psalm and ask who it speaks of. Inner reading: A leader who needs this verse not to be questioned has already answered the question.

resposta: Malachi 3:10 Bring all the tithes into the treasury, and try me now, if I will not open unto you the windows of heaven. And 3:8-9: ye rob me in the tithes; ye are cursed with the curse. It's used to say that whoever doesn't tithe to the church is stealing from God and cursed. User's answer: The principle of honoring God with possessions still holds.
aprofundar: Context: The prophet speaks to the nation of Israel under the Mosaic Law some five hundred years before Christ. The tithe was in produce of the land, kept in the temple storehouse, so that there would be food in my house, and it sustained the Levites, who had no land; Nehemiah 13:10 shows the crisis when they did not receive. The New Testament does not command Christians to tithe; Paul, at 2 Corinthians 9:7, calls for a voluntary offering: each contributes as he has purposed in his heart; not with sorrow or under compulsion. How to protect yourself: Be suspicious of any promise of financial return in exchange for an offer, and hold the church accountable. Inner reading: Giving can be a beautiful act; giving out of fear of cursing is an imposed exchange.

resposta: Ephesians 5:22: Wives, be in subjection to your own husbands as to the Lord. It's used to keep women in abusive marriages. But the preceding verse, 5:21, says: "Be in subjection to one another in fear of Christ"; and 5:25 commands: "Husbands, continue loving your wives, just as the Christ also loved the congregation and delivered up himself for it". Answer: It is God's arrangement for the family, and the husband is the head.
aprofundar: The context: Paul writes within the Roman domestic code, in which the husband had almost total power, and he transforms it: Submission is mutual, and the pattern of the husband is to surrender, not dominate. No verse commands a woman to accept violence. Theologians of all stripes, including conservatives, claim that abuse breaks the covenant. How to protect yourself: In the event of violence, call 180, the Women's Health Center, or 190; no religion asks that you accept to be hurt. Inner reading: A verse quoted without neighbors becomes a chain; read whole, it is a limit against power.

tema: Servants, obey - the Bible of the slave masters

resposta: Ephesians 6:5: Slaves, obey those who are your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling. Colossians 3:22 repeats: be obedient in all things. And Genesis 9:25, cursed be Canaan, servant of servants, was read, without reference to the text, as the curse of Ham and the Africans. These verses sustained sermons to enslaved people in the Americas. The wearer's answer: Slavery was a divine order and obedience a Christian virtue.
aprofundar: What is proven: There was a Slave Bible, published in London in 1807 for use in the colonies, which cut out most of the Exodus and passages that spoke of freedom. Genesis 9:25 curses Canaan, and it does not mention color or Africa. And Paul, at Galatians 3:28, says: There is neither slave nor free; you are all one in Christ Jesus. How to protect yourself: When a scripture is used to say that a group was born to serve, read the entire chapter and the story of who used it. Inner reading: the one who has power chooses the verses; the one who wants freedom reads the whole book.
camada3: To reflect: If someone had to cut out Exodus from the Bible to control people, what does that say about the liberating power of the entire text?

resposta: Romans 13:1-2: Let every soul be in subjection to the superior authorities, for there is no authority except that which comes from God; the one who opposes the authority has taken a stand against the arrangement of God. It was used to support the Nazi regime, apartheid in South Africa and dictatorships, including in Latin America. User's Answer: Order and government are God's institutions, and the Christian must obey.
aprofundar: Background: Paul was writing to a small community in Rome that needed to escape persecution. The text itself says, at 13:3, that magistrates are a cause for fear, not to those doing good, but to those doing bad. And at Acts 5:29, Peter and the apostles, arrested for preaching, answer: We must obey God as ruler rather than men. Christians like Dietrich Bonhoeffer, executed in 1945, resisted Nazism because of their faith. How to protect yourself: Civil obedience is different from obedience to injustice; your conscience remains yours. Inside reading: Anyone who uses Romans 13 to silence their conscience forgets that the Bible is full of prophets who disobeyed unjust kings.
camada3: To ponder: Is there a limit to obedience? Where's yours?

They are used to demand total obedience to leaders and to isolate anyone who asks or leaves, severing friendships and even family ties. Answer: The church has spiritual authority and must correct to protect the flock.
aprofundar: Context: Hebrews speaks of guides who watch over souls and will render an account, not of conscience holders. Matthew 18 describes a way of reconciliation between brothers for a real sin, alone first, and Jesus was rightly criticized for eating with publicans and sinners, as at Matthew 9:11. The Bible also commands: "Test everything out", at 1 Thessalonians 5:21. How to protect yourself: Keep your ties out of the group, and be wary of any community that forbids you from talking to your outsider. Internal reading: a reconciliation text used as an exclusion weapon is one of the hallmarks of group control that the Portal describes in Pandora's Box.

resposta: Rev. 21:8 But the cowardly, the unbelieving, the vile, the murderers, and all liars - their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death. It's used to terrorize those who doubt or want to leave the church. User response: Hell is real, and warning is an act of love.

Christians have different readings of hell: eternal torment, annihilation, the hope of universal salvation; it is tradition and interpretation, not proven fact. resposta: 2 Timothy 3:16: All Scripture is divinely inspired and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness. It is used to say that every word of a modern translation is dictated by God, and that any question is rebellion. User's answer: If the Bible is inspired, it cannot be in error at all.

The text says what Scripture is for, teaching and correcting, not the absence of copying errors. The church itself acknowledges copying errors, such as Ahaziah's age. resposta: After seeing contradictions, atrocities and verses used to manipulate, the Portal's conclusion is not to throw the Bible away, nor to pretend none of that is there. It's reading the whole book, with context, with history and with questions. Acts 17:11 commends the Beroeans, who examined the Scriptures daily as to whether these things were so, including what the apostle was saying. And 1 Thessalonians 5:21 sums it up: Make sure of all things; hold fast to what is fine.
aprofundar: How to do it: Read an entire book at once, like a letter. Ask who wrote, to whom, when and why. Compare translations, and when you can, consult a scholarly study Bible. Separate what the text says God did, what it says humans did, and what interpreters say today. And look who profits from the reading they taught you. grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Who created the Trinity: the timeline
palavras: father son and holy spirit origin
origin of the father son and holy spirit
who created the trinity the timeline
pai filho e espirito santo origem
origem do pai filho e espirito santo
resposta: The Trinity was not created by one person, nor in a single day. It was formulated over some three hundred years. The New Testament already has formulas with three names, such as baptizing in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, in Matthew 28:19, but it does not explain the doctrine. The word Trinity appears around 180, with Theophilus of Antioch, and in Latin, Trinitas, around 213, with Tertullian. The official definitions came in two councils: Nicaea, in 325, about the Son, and Constantinople, in 381, about the Holy Spirit.
aprofundar: The timeline: around 55, Paul writes the blessing of the grace of Jesus, the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, in 2 Corinthians 13:14, which in some Bibles is 13:13. Around 100, the Didache, an early Christian manual, repeats the baptism formula in three names. Around 112, the Roman governor Pliny the Younger tells the emperor that Christians sang hymns to Christ as to a god. Around 213, Tertullian writes Against Praxeas and speaks of one substance and three persons. In the third century, Origen uses the word hypostasis, but places the Son below the Father. Around 318, the priest Arius says the Son was created, and the great dispute begins. In 325, Nicaea declares the Son of the same substance as the Father, but about the Spirit it says only: and in the Holy Spirit. Between 360 and 380, the Cappadocian Fathers, Basil and the two Gregories, establish the formula of one essence and three persons. In 381, Constantinople completes the creed about the Spirit. Then come the Athanasian Creed, written in Latin in the fifth or sixth century, and not by Athanasius; and the Filioque, the phrase and the Son, added in the West from 589 onward and one of the reasons for the split between Rome and the East, in 1054. The theologians' answer: the doctrine was not invented; it was a way of explaining what the first Christians already lived when they worshipped the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Practice: when you hear that something was always this way, ask when it was written, by whom and in the middle of which dispute.
camada3: To contemplate: an idea that took three hundred years and many councils to be defined, is it a finished revelation, or the human search to explain the mystery? Both answers can fit in the same faith; what does not fit is pretending there was no history.

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: Is the Trinity in the Bible?
palavras: is the trinity in the bible
does the bible talk about the trinity
the trinity is not in the bible
resposta: The word Trinity does not appear anywhere in the Bible, and neither does the phrase three persons and one essence. That is a fact. What exists are texts that speak of the Father, the Son and the Spirit together, and texts that call Jesus God, such as John 1:1 and John 20:28. There are also texts that seem to place the Son below the Father, such as John 14:28: the Father is greater than I.
aprofundar: How each side reads it: defenders of the Trinity say the doctrine gathers the pieces scattered through the Bible, like someone putting together a puzzle. Critics say the pieces were fitted with tools from Greek philosophy, such as the words essence and person, which the biblical authors did not use. Another text often cited by critics is Mark 13:32, where Jesus says that not even the Son knows the day of the end, only the Father. Throughout history, many sincere Christians did not accept the Trinity: the Arians in the fourth century; Michael Servetus, burned in Geneva in 1553 for denying the Trinity; the Unitarians; and today Jehovah's Witnesses and Oneness Pentecostals, each with their own reading. In other words, doubt about the Trinity is old within Christianity itself. The theologians' answer: not every truth of faith needs a technical word in the Bible; the word came later to protect what was believed. Practice: read John 1, John 14 and Mark 13 in full and write down what the text says, before what you were told it says.
camada3: To contemplate: if sincere Christians have disagreed about this for seventeen centuries, what does that say about those who claim that doubting the Trinity means certain damnation?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
palavras: the trinity was created by constantine
resposta: Myth. Constantine did not create the Trinity. The word Trinity is more than a hundred years older than him. At Nicaea, in 325, which he convened, the question was whether the Son was of the same substance as the Father; the Holy Spirit was barely discussed. The part of the creed about the Spirit was only defined in 381, in Constantinople, under the emperor Theodosius, forty-four years after Constantine's death.
aprofundar: What Constantine really did: he legalized Christianity in 313, convened and pressured the Council of Nicaea to end the dispute that divided the empire, and exiled those who did not sign. But later he changed sides: he called Arius back, exiled Athanasius, the greatest defender of Nicaea, in 335, and was baptized on his deathbed, in 337, by Eusebius of Nicomedia, an Arian bishop. His son, Constantius the Second, supported the Arians. In other words, Constantine's family helped the side that denied the equality of the Son more than the side of the Trinity. What is true in this suspicion: imperial power entered theology, and from then on disagreeing with the official doctrine could cost exile, and later life itself. In 380, Theodosius made Nicene Christianity the official religion and called the others heretics. The theologians' answer: the council only put into words a faith that already existed, and the emperor did not decide the content. Practice: always separate two questions: who invented an idea, and who used power to impose it.
camada3: To contemplate: the myth that an emperor invented everything is simpler than the truth, and the truth is more serious: faith was married to the sword. What changes in you when you know this?

Pagan trinities: plagiarism or parallel?

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
resposta: Triads of gods exist in many cultures, and that is real. In Egypt, Osiris, Isis and Horus form a family: father, mother and son. In Rome, Jupiter, Juno and Minerva were the Capitoline Triad. In India, the Trimurti unites Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. But the idea that the Christian Trinity is a direct copy of one of them is not accepted by most historians. Pagan triads are almost always three different gods; the Trinity says one God in three persons, and it was born among Jews who swore there was only one God.
aprofundar: What is a real parallel: the number three is sacred in almost every culture, and the psychologist Carl Jung saw an archetype in triads. An Egyptian hymn from Leiden, from around 1213 before Christ, says that all the gods are three, Amun, Ra and Ptah, and that the three are one; it is the closest parallel. In philosophy, Philo of Alexandria, a Jew of the first century, called the Logos, the Word, a second God; and Plotinus, who lived from 204 to 270, taught three principles: the One, the Intellect and the Soul. This Greek vocabulary influenced Christian theologians; that is accepted by research. What does not hold up: the Trimurti was organized in the Purana texts, from the fourth century after Christ onward, so it could not be the source; and the famous Babylonian trinity of Nimrod, Semiramis and Tammuz comes from the book The Two Babylons, by Alexander Hislop, from 1853, full of errors; the pastor Ralph Woodrow, who had written a book based on it, later refuted it and withdrew his own book. The theologians' answer: similarity of language is not copying; Christians used Greek words to explain a Jewish experience. Practice: when faced with a parallel, ask who came first, whether there is a document linking the two, and whether the similarity is of form or of content.
camada3: To contemplate: if all of humanity draws the sacred in threes, perhaps that says something about the human mind, and not about who copied whom. The truth does not need plagiarism to be questioned, nor originality to be lived.

The sum of history

tema: 1 John 5:7: the Trinity verse that was added
palavras: three that bear record in heaven
the father the word and the holy ghost and these three are one
1 john 5 7 the trinity verse that was added
o pai a palavra e o espirito santo e estes tres sao um
resposta: The only verse in the Bible that says almost in so many words that the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit are one is 1 John 5:7. And it was added. The phrase about the three that bear record in heaven does not appear in any ancient Greek manuscript; the oldest one that has it is from the fourteenth century. That is why modern translations such as the NIV leave this passage out, or only mention it in a footnote. The King James Version still keeps it.
aprofundar: The history: the phrase first appears in Latin texts, around 380, linked to the bishop Priscillian, and probably began as a comment in the margin that later entered the text. Erasmus did not include it in the first two editions of his Greek New Testament, was accused of favoring the Arians, and included it in the third, in 1522, after a Greek manuscript containing it turned up, probably made to order at that time. That is how it entered the Textus Receptus and the old Bibles. Isaac Newton wrote a study of this alteration in 1690, published only after his death. In 1897, Rome forbade questioning the verse; in 1927, it reversed course and allowed research. Today Catholics, Protestants and secular scholars agree: it is not original. The theologians' answer: the Trinity does not depend on this verse; it was defined without it. Practice: open 1 John 5:7 and 8 in two translations, the King James Version and the NIV, and compare with your own eyes.
camada3: To contemplate: someone thought the truth needed a little help and wrote into the Bible what they wanted to read in it. How many of your certainties were also written in the margin by someone else?

tema: The sin against the Holy Spirit and the fear of not being forgiven
palavras: i sinned against the holy spirit
did i sin against the holy spirit
the sin against the holy spirit and the fear of not being forgiven
sera que pequei contra o espirito santo
resposta: Jesus says in Matthew 12:31 and 32, and in Mark 3:28 and 29, that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven. Hebrews 6:4 to 6 speaks of those who fell away and cannot be renewed. These verses are used to instill fear: if you doubt, leave the church or think something bad, you may have committed the sin of no return. Psychology knows this fear well: it is called scrupulosity, a form of obsessive-compulsive disorder with a religious theme, and it can be treated.
aprofundar: The context: in Mark 3:30, the text explains why Jesus said it: because they said he had an unclean spirit, that is, they called good evil. It was not about a thought that slips out, nor about a sincere doubt. The philosopher Bertrand Russell, in Why I Am Not a Christian, from 1927, said this verse caused an unspeakable amount of misery in the world, because many people came to believe they had committed it. A famous example is John Bunyan, author of The Pilgrim's Progress, who tells of living tormented by this fear for years. The research: a 2006 study from the Mayo Clinic, with OCD patients, linked scrupulosity to the belief that thoughts must be controlled and to thought-action fusion, the idea that thinking something bad is as serious as doing it. The most studied treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy with exposure and response prevention, which has been adapted even for very religious people. The theologians' answer: most pastors and priests say that anyone afraid of having committed this sin shows precisely that they have not, because they still care about God; the Catholic Catechism defines it as refusing mercy forever. Practice: if a religious thought traps you in cycles of fear, guilt and rituals to find relief, this has a name and it can be treated; see a psychologist.
camada3: To contemplate: a text about not calling good evil became a weapon to call doubt a crime. Who profits when you are afraid to think?

tema: Where the hell of fire came from
palavras: is hell in the hebrew bible
where the hell of fire came from
resposta: The hell of eternal fire is not in the Hebrew Bible. Sheol was the dark place of all the dead, good and bad, without torture. The idea of eternal punishment formed gradually: it appears faintly in Daniel 12:2, around 165 before Christ, and grows in the Jewish apocalyptic books, such as First Enoch, between the third and first centuries before Christ. In the New Testament, Jesus speaks of Gehenna, the name of the Valley of Hinnom, near Jerusalem, where according to Jeremiah 7:31 children had been burned in sacrifice.
aprofundar: The influences: many scholars see Persian influence, because Zoroastrianism already had a final judgment, a bridge of the dead and a place of punishment, and the Jews lived under the Persians between 539 and 332 before Christ; this is a debated hypothesis, not a settled fact. The Greek influence is clearer: Hades and Tartarus, the prison of the Titans; 2 Peter 2:4 uses a verb that means to cast into Tartarus. A common myth: that Gehenna was a garbage dump that was always burning. That explanation only appears around 1200, with the rabbi David Kimhi, and archaeology does not confirm it. Then came imagination: the Apocalypse of Peter, from the second century, describes detailed tortures; Augustine, in the fifth century, defends eternal and literal fire; Dante, between 1308 and 1321, draws hell in nine circles; and the preacher Jonathan Edwards, in 1741, in the sermon Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God, compares the listener to a spider held over the fire. The theologians' answer: revelation is progressive, and Jesus would have revealed what was hidden before. Practice: when you imagine hell, ask where each image comes from: from the Bible, from Dante, or from a sermon.
camada3: To contemplate: the hell that frightens you has the face of which century? Much of what people fear is not in the text; it is in the painting someone made of it.

tema: Infinite punishment for a finite mistake?
palavras: infinite punishment for a finite mistake
resposta: This is the so-called problem of hell, debated for centuries by philosophers, including Christians. The argument: a human life is short and limited, so no mistake in it could deserve endless suffering. The philosopher David Hume asked, in an essay published in 1777: why then eternal punishment for the temporary offences of so frail a creature as man? A punishment should be proportionate to the offense.
aprofundar: More voices: Hume also pointed out that a punishment without purpose, when it can no longer correct or protect anyone, does not fit our idea of goodness. Bertrand Russell called the doctrine of hell fire a doctrine of cruelty. The Christian philosopher Marilyn McCord Adams, in 1993, said that a God who created people knowing they would suffer forever would not be good to them. The Christian philosopher Thomas Talbott, in 1999, in the book The Inescapable Love of God, argues that God's love ends up winning everyone over. The classic answers: Augustine, in The City of God, defended eternal punishment against those he called the merciful ones. Anselm and Thomas Aquinas argued that the gravity of an offense depends on the dignity of the one offended, and offending an infinite God would be an infinite offense. C. S. Lewis, in The Problem of Pain, from 1940, said that the damned are, in a sense, rebels to the end, and that the doors of hell are locked on the inside: God would not imprison anyone; the person would refuse to leave. The critics reply: in no just court is punishment ever measured by the dignity of the victim, and a child, or someone who never heard of God, does not choose hell with full awareness. Practice: read one argument from each side and notice which one requires you to switch off your sense of justice.
camada3: To contemplate: if a human father burned his son forever for one mistake, no one would call him just. Why would we accept from God a moral standard worse than our own? And, with respect for those who believe: what if your conscience, which revolts against this, is the best of God in you?

tema: Eternal hell is not the only Christian reading
palavras: eternal hell is not the only reading
eternal hell is not the only christian reading
inferno eterno nao e a unica leitura
resposta: Many people do not know it, but eternal torment was never the only Christian reading. There are three main positions. The first, eternal torment, is the most common in Catholicism and Protestantism. The second, annihilationism or conditional immortality, says that those who reject God cease to exist; it was defended, cautiously, by the Anglican pastor John Stott, in 1988. The third, universalism, says that in the end everyone will be reconciled with God.
aprofundar: Universalism has ancient roots: Origen, in the third century, and Gregory of Nyssa, in the fourth century, one of the very Fathers who defined the Trinity, hoped for the restoration of all, the apokatastasis. Isaac of Nineveh, in the seventh century, said that hell is the love of God felt as torment by those who refuse it. In 2019, the Orthodox theologian David Bentley Hart published That All Shall Be Saved, arguing that the Greek word translated as eternal, aionios, means of an age, and not necessarily without end. The official Catholic position, in the Catechism, affirms hell and its eternity, but Pope John Paul the Second, in 1999, explained that hell is not a punishment imposed externally by God, but the state of those who freely separate themselves from him, more a state than a place. The Catholic theologian Hans Urs von Balthasar argued that it is legitimate to hope that hell is empty. The Orthodox also vary. The answer of those who defend eternal torment: Matthew 25:46 puts eternal punishment beside eternal life, and if one is endless, the other would be too. Practice: if you were taught that there is only one reading, know that people of faith, holy and learned, thought differently.
camada3: To contemplate: if even the saints disagreed about hell, is the one who threatens you with it as absolute certainty speaking for God, or for themselves?

tema: Phobia indoctrination: fear of hell as a leash
palavras: phobia indoctrination fear of hell as a leash
resposta: Fear is one of the most studied tools of control. The cult expert Steven Hassan created the BITE model, which looks at four kinds of control: of behavior, of information, of thought and of emotions. Within emotional control is what he calls phobia indoctrination: implanting fears so strong that the person cannot even imagine leaving the group, such as going to hell, losing salvation or being destroyed. This can happen in any group; it is not an attack on anyone's faith.
aprofundar: What the research shows: in 2014, the psychologists Azim Shariff and Lara Aknin, in three studies, found that believing in heaven is linked to more happiness, while believing in hell is linked to less happiness and less life satisfaction; and just thinking about hell already worsened mood. Honesty: a 2012 study, by the same Shariff, found that countries where more people believe in hell have fewer crimes. In other words, fear works to control behavior; that is exactly why it is used, and it does not prove that hell exists. As early as 1777, Hume wrote that the terrors about the afterlife would soon vanish if they were not fostered by education, and asked what motive those who foster them have. The psychiatrist Robert Lifton called the dispensing of existence the idea that those outside the group do not deserve to exist. The theologians' answer: warning of a real danger is love, not manipulation; the problem is when the warning becomes a threat to obey the leader. Practice: when you feel religious fear, ask: who told me this, what do they gain if I obey, and can I verify it?
camada3: To contemplate: a fear that cannot be verified, but that forces you to obey someone who can, is it faith or a leash? The faith that sets free does not need bars.

tema: Would a God of love be an executioner?
palavras: would a god of love be an executioner
how can god send people to hell
if god is love why is there hell
como deus pode mandar para o inferno
se deus e amor por que existe inferno
o perfeito amor lanca fora o medo
resposta: This is the most important question, and the Bible itself provides material for it. 1 John 4:18 says: there is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear. Ezekiel 18:23 and 32 says that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that he turn and live. 1 Timothy 2:4 says that God wants all people to be saved. A being who gives life and then tortures forever those who went wrong does not match this portrait.
aprofundar: Adding up the pieces: a loving father does not burn his son; a just judge gives a proportionate sentence; a doctor does not punish forever the patient who did not get well. Lamentations 3:31 to 33 says that the Lord does not cast off forever and does not willingly afflict. In the parable of the prodigal son, in Luke 15:20, the father runs to meet his son even before he asks for forgiveness. And 1 Corinthians 15:28 speaks of God being all in all. That is why many Christians conclude that the image of a torturing God comes more from human fear and religious power than from the love Jesus preached. The answer of theologians who defend hell: love also means respecting freedom; God forces no one to love him, and hell would be the person's final choice, not God's revenge. The critics reply: a choice made without full knowledge, out of fear, out of trauma or because of being born into another religion, is not truly a free choice. No one can prove what exists after death; that is unknown. Practice: read the whole of 1 John 4 and ask whether the God you were taught fits in it.
camada3: To contemplate: if you, with all your flaws, could not torture even your worst enemy forever, your heart has already answered the question. Perhaps God is greater than the fear you were taught about him.

grupo: Contradições, Atrocidades e Manipulação na Bíblia
tema: The final sum: truth, myth and manipulation
palavras: what is true about the trinity
what is a lie about hell
the final sum truth, myth and manipulation
o que e verdade sobre a trindade
o que e mentira sobre o inferno
o que e manipulacao na religiao
resposta: Adding it all up. It is proven truth: the word Trinity is not in the Bible; the doctrine was formulated between the second and fourth centuries, with Tertullian, Nicaea, in 325, and Constantinople, in 381; 1 John 5:7 was added; the hell of fire does not exist in the Hebrew Bible and took shape over time. It is myth: that Constantine invented the Trinity, and that it is a direct copy of a pagan trinity. It is manipulation: using the fear of hell and of the unforgivable sin to prevent questions and ensure obedience.
aprofundar: More details of the sum. Proven: the images of hell were expanded by Dante, in 1321, and by sermons like that of Jonathan Edwards, in 1741; and believing in hell is linked to lower well-being. Hypothesis: the Persian influence on the final judgment and the influence of Greek philosophy on the vocabulary of the Trinity; the second is widely accepted, the first is debated. Tradition: the Trinity, eternal hell, annihilation and the salvation of all are beliefs of faith; sincere Christians have defended each of them. Unknown: what exists after death; no one can prove hell, nor prove that it does not exist. Where the suspicion is right: the doctrine has a human history, it was backed by the power of the empire, and the fear of hell is used to control. Where history corrects: the Trinity was not born from Constantine nor from plagiarism; it was born from debates among Christians trying to explain their faith. The theologians' answer: that the doctrine has a history does not prove it is false; many truths were discovered little by little. Practice: keep this sum and use the same method for any belief: what is document, what is assumption, what is faith and what is fear.
camada3: To contemplate: freeing yourself from fear does not require hating anyone's faith. It only requires knowing how to separate what is history, what is mystery and what is a leash. What, in this sum, changed inside you?

palavras: how to lose the fear of hell
how to overcome the fear of hell
i can t stop being afraid of hell
como perder o medo do inferno
como superar o medo do inferno
medo de ir para o inferno
nao consigo parar de ter medo do inferno
resposta: Leaving the fear of hell behind does not happen all at once, and it does not have to be done with anger. The fear was learned, often in childhood, and the brain learns again with time and repetition. Three paths help: understanding the history, as in these lessons; caring for body and mind, with a psychologist; and replacing the voice of punishment with a voice of kindness toward yourself.
aprofundar: What the research supports: self-compassion, studied by the psychologist Kristin Neff, is treating yourself the way you would treat a dear friend who is suffering. A 2012 meta-analysis, by MacBeth and Gumley, brought together fourteen studies and found a strong link between more self-compassion and less anxiety, depression and stress; it is a link, not proof of cause. For those who live in cycles of obsessive religious thoughts, therapy with exposure and response prevention is the most studied treatment. Care: look for a licensed psychologist, whose registration you can check with the professional board (in Brazil, the Federal Council of Psychology), and who respects your faith or your lack of it. You do not need to abandon your faith to leave fear behind; many people find a faith based on love. If the suffering becomes too heavy, in Brazil call one eight eight, the CVV, free, at any time; in other countries, call your local crisis line. The theologians' answer: many pastors and priests also condemn preaching through terror and recall Matthew 11:28 to 30: come to me, and I will give you rest. Practice: when the fear of hell comes, breathe deeply three times, put your hand on your chest and say: this is a fear I was taught; I can look at it calmly.
camada3: To contemplate: fear taught you that you had to earn not being burned. What if the truth is simpler: that you deserve peace just for existing?
